locator: §6.3, Dummett, 'the central notion in the theory of meaning for mathematics is not, as in Platonism, truth, but proof'
interpretation: Attribution reading of Dummett's position as the entry reports it: meaning is use, so 'the central notion in the theory of meaning for mathematics is not, as in Platonism, truth, but proof; the understanding of a mathematical statement consists in the ability to recognize a proof of it when one is presented with one'. Formalized as the anti-realist biconditional 'p holds exactly when p is proved at some stage' (TruthCore.English.Iemhoff.TruthIsProvabilityReading). That formula is stronger than the sentence, which states the primacy of proof in a theory of meaning; it is the intuitionist account put in the place of proof-transcendent truth, as the owner principle requires a rival to supply, and the claim flags it as the most contestable reading. Like the entry, it concerns mathematical statements; extending it to all propositions is the comparison's step.
